input.summary:
P0 front room furnished inside [4,3,10,7,6,12]: birch table (fence post + top slab) with two birch stair chairs, a lit west-facing smoker by the east chimney at (7,3,12), a barrel dresser with a potted poppy, and a lit candle on the table. Paths stay clear from the front door (x5..6) to the partition door (x5, z13).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the room line shows 9 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE. The room check shows min light 9 with 0 dark cells and fit OK; the walk is UNREACHABLE only because the front steps, door and porch rails (Fittings) are still stubs.
Source is parts/room-1.mjs, layers() draws it; room.png was read and the table, chairs and smoker read as a living room.
left: Walkability not verified by the tool: `$MCD room` reports UNREACHABLE because the front door, step and porch rails from Fittings are not built yet. By reading the grid, x5..6 at z10..12 and x5 at z13 are clear, and the table, chairs, barrel and smoker are each reachable from an adjacent clear cell. Re-run `$MCD room` after Fittings lands to confirm OK.

Lighting: the spec asked for a lantern hung from the plate, but I used a lit candle on the table. A hanging lantern needs a block above it at y7 inside the room, and the roof part is still a stub, so I could not confirm one. Light is already min 9 with the lit smoker (13) and the candle, so a lantern is optional. If the roof leaves y7 solid, hang one at (5,6,11) from iron_chain.
Floor: the spec said birch-plank floor, but the shell's floor deck is oak_planks at y2, outside my box, so I did not change it. Birch would need a shell change or a carpet on top.
Smoker at (7,3,12) is also in the Hearths stove list (RESERVED). If Hearths places it first, my write is refused by runParts. That is harmless, but Hearths should keep the same state (west, lit).
Plan.md checklist and elements.md have no room-level ticks, so nothing was ticked. I did not edit shared files, to avoid racing the parallel workers.

waste.what: Drew the furniture as three layers of 4-character rows and worked out each chair's facing and each slab/fence stacking by hand, cell by cell.
waste.cost: About 6 cell decisions and 2 rebuild cycles; the rows were written once and only the lighting was retried.
waste.tool: A room-furnishing helper that takes a named layout (focal piece, table with N chairs, dresser against a wall) and emits the layers() text with facings and stacking already correct.

waste.what: Checked each block id against palette.json by reading the file and grepping roles, instead of running `$MCD blocks --check` on the list.
waste.cost: About 8 ids checked by eye, with one grep.
waste.tool: `$MCD palette-check <room.json>` or a palette-aware layers() that refuses off-palette ids before the build.

waste.what: Could not confirm the walk verdict; the only check was reading the grid, because the door and steps come from Fittings.
waste.cost: One extra room check run, and a manual reachability read of the floor grid.
waste.tool: `$MCD room --assume-open-doors` (or a walk from the room's own openings) so a room can be verified before the shell's entry parts land.

waste.what: Decided on the candle-versus-lantern lighting by reasoning about whether the y7 ceiling is solid; no tool reports what is above the room.
waste.cost: Two lamp options considered, no build test.
waste.tool: `$MCD room` lamp suggestions should list which hanging anchors (blocks at y+1) actually exist in the current build.

companions.task: Decide the hanging lantern from the head plate once the roof part shows whether y7 above the room is solid, and check that the light map still reads 8+ with the candle removed.
Build the table and the two chairs as proper joinery from the same birch stock as the walls, so the chairs' back and seat faces are right the first time.
Lay a white_carpet rug under the table between the chairs and the door path, which would give the front room its focal ground.

structured_output.summary:
P0 front room furnished inside [4,3,10,7,6,12]: birch table (fence post + top slab) with two birch stair chairs, a lit west-facing smoker by the east chimney at (7,3,12), a barrel dresser with a potted poppy, and a lit candle on the table. Paths stay clear from the front door (x5..6) to the partition door (x5, z13).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the room line shows 9 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE. The room check shows min light 9 with 0 dark cells and fit OK; the walk is UNREACHABLE only because the front steps, door and porch rails (Fittings) are still stubs.
Source is parts/room-1.mjs, layers() draws it; room.png was read and the table, chairs and smoker read as a living room.
left: Walkability not verified by the tool: `$MCD room` reports UNREACHABLE because the front door, step and porch rails from Fittings are not built yet. By reading the grid, x5..6 at z10..12 and x5 at z13 are clear, and the table, chairs, barrel and smoker are each reachable from an adjacent clear cell. Re-run `$MCD room` after Fittings lands to confirm OK.

Lighting: the spec asked for a lantern hung from the plate, but I used a lit candle on the table. A hanging lantern needs a block above it at y7 inside the room, and the roof part is still a stub, so I could not confirm one. Light is already min 9 with the lit smoker (13) and the candle, so a lantern is optional. If the roof leaves y7 solid, hang one at (5,6,11) from iron_chain.
Floor: the spec said birch-plank floor, but the shell's floor deck is oak_planks at y2, outside my box, so I did not change it. Birch would need a shell change or a carpet on top.
Smoker at (7,3,12) is also in the Hearths stove list (RESERVED). If Hearths places it first, my write is refused by runParts. That is harmless, but Hearths should keep the same state (west, lit).
Plan.md checklist and elements.md have no room-level ticks, so nothing was ticked. I did not edit shared files, to avoid racing the parallel workers.

waste.what: Drew the furniture as three layers of 4-character rows and worked out each chair's facing and each slab/fence stacking by hand, cell by cell.

waste.tool: A room-furnishing helper that takes a named layout (focal piece, table with N chairs, dresser against a wall) and emits the layers() text with facings and stacking already correct.
